absences: No fuel-supply or financing event dated after 2026-10-30 surfaced across 10 angles. Newest matches were all before the window: Radiant and Antares TRISO deals with Standard Nuclear (2026-08-20 and 2026-08-27), Centrus and Radiant HALEU MOU (2026-09-12), Last Energy EXIM letter of interest (undated in results). Items: none.
FY2024 PCE order (pce.akenergyauthority.org FY24 Base Rate Change Final L2300184.pdf) could not be read: WebFetch returned a binary stream. The shipped 19.35 cents/kWh figure is therefore unverified.
FY2026 PCE base of 20.38 cents/kWh appears only in a search summary (docket U-25-010 opening order and AEA consumer page). The final FY2026 order was not found or fetched, so it is not cited.
The FY2027 proposal of 22.11 cents/kWh is a proposal (notice dated 2026-05-01, responses due 2026-06-02). No final order was found, so the in-force base is not confirmed.
Morgan Lewis OBBBA summary (July 2025) confirms the 2034 begin-construction deadline and three-year phase-out for nuclear under 45Y/48E. It is a secondary source, so no check was written.

arXiv 2506.13361 v2 (2025-12-19) abstract states a PTC LCOE range of $48.21 to $78.32/MWh and a 22-24% PTC reduction, matching shipped figures. Not emitted: the fetch output carried escaped dollar signs, so a verbatim quote could not be confirmed.

Not checked (no fetched primary source obtained): HALEU and TRISO unit prices and DOE allocation values, enrichment contract values, diesel and fuel-oil delivered prices in remote markets, insurance, staffing (INL $178,500 per staff-year and Michigan $120,000-$225,000 figures), and the INL RPT-25-87273 tool figures.
The DOE HALEU allocation page for the third round (NASA and Radiant, reported July 2026) was not fetched. The 21 MT NDAA target status is unverified.

checks.claim: The PCE base rate, set at 19.35 cents/kWh ...
checks.evidence: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska notice dated 1 May 2026 (docket U-26-010) proposes to revise the PCE base amount to 22.11 cents/kWh for the FY2027 calculation. It is a proposal, not a final order, and responses were due 2 June 2026. The 19.35 figure is not the base the 2026 notice describes as current.

checks.review: Overruled: the shipped sentence already says '19.35 cents/kWh in 2023, was 20.38 cents/kWh in 2026 (22.11 proposed for FY2027)'. The agent quoted only the first clause.
